strings.name: Donna Strickland
strings.summary: As a doctoral student at Rochester, Donna Strickland developed chirped-pulse amplification with her supervisor Gérard Mourou: stretching a pulse, amplifying it and compressing it again to reduce damage during amplification. The method advanced intense ultrashort lasers and influenced precision manufacturing and eye surgery. She continued ultrafast and nonlinear-optics research at Waterloo and shared half the 2018 Nobel Prize in Physics with Mourou.
strings.coverageNote: Research checked through 13 November 2026; selected milestones extend to 2018. This is not a daily news archive. Shared achievements are credited to collaborators and teams.
strings.influence.rationale: Co-developed chirped pulse amplification, advancing high-intensity laser applications in research, industry and medicine.

strings.facts.fact-2.label: Education

strings.highlights.highlight-1.title: Chirped-pulse amplification
strings.highlights.highlight-1.text: With Mourou, developed stretching, amplification and recompression to amplify ultrashort pulses at higher energies.
strings.highlights.highlight-2.title: Ultrafast and nonlinear optics
strings.highlights.highlight-2.text: Studies intense laser–matter interactions, multifrequency Raman processes and sources in new wavelength ranges.
strings.timeline.event-1.title: Nobel Prize in Physics
strings.timeline.event-1.text: Shared half the prize with Mourou for generating intense ultrashort pulses; Arthur Ashkin received the other half.
strings.timeline.event-2.title: Optical Society president
strings.timeline.event-2.text: Served as OSA president, contributing to the optics research community.
strings.timeline.event-3.title: Joined Waterloo
strings.timeline.event-3.text: Developed an ultrafast-laser research program on high-intensity systems and nonlinear-optics experiments.
strings.timeline.event-4.title: Lawrence Livermore research
strings.timeline.event-4.text: Moved to laser research in the United States after work at Canada's National Research Council.
strings.timeline.event-5.title: Optics doctorate
strings.timeline.event-5.text: Completed her Rochester doctorate after research that included chirped-pulse amplification.
strings.timeline.event-6.title: Chirped-pulse paper
strings.timeline.event-6.text: Published the amplification and compression method with Mourou, establishing a basis for intense ultrafast lasers.
strings.timeline.event-7.title: Engineering-physics degree
strings.timeline.event-7.text: Graduated from McMaster before graduate study in optics at Rochester.
strings.timeline.event-8.title: Born in Guelph
